solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Island with a snack from the East

parts.note: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean

explanation.surface: A traveller lands on a Greek island and picks up something oriental to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried, triangular pastry parcel originating in South Asian cooking, eaten as a light bite.

clue.text: A provider of room associated with keys?

definitions.text: A provider of room associated with keys?

parts.words: A provider of room associated with keys?
parts.note: sounds like a landlord with door keys, but it is the long bar on a keyboard that makes gaps between words

explanation.surface: A landlord who hands over the keys along with lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key at the foot of a keyboard inserts blank gaps when typing.

clue.text: Month associated with German saying

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German proverb tied to a particular month of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: A short maxim or slogan adopted as a guiding principle is a kind of saying.

clue.text: Opt to wander in closed athletics event

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled letters inside the closed word

parts.note: shut means closed

indicators.note: to wander is to stray from the set path, so the letters of opt are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spectator chooses to wander into a closed sports meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closed' reads as describing the event, but it is a synonym that wraps round the jumbled letters (OTP) that 'wander' makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a heavy metal ball for distance is a field discipline at track meets.

clue.text: Plant firm put back beset by a lot of press

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the shortened press word goes round the reversed firm
a lot of, not all, so the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to press is to crush

indicators.note: put back tells us the letters for firm are read backwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company's factory gets swamped by a heavy machine press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers; here it is a verb synonym. 'a lot of' cuts its last letter, and 'put back' turns the firm round to OC.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spring-flowering bulb with cup-shaped blooms, a common garden flower.

clue.text: Painter around island showing coastal region

indicators.note: around means the painter's name surrounds the island letter

parts.note: Diego Rivera was a Mexican painter

explanation.surface: A painter on an island reveals the shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: The French and Italian Mediterranean seaboard is a stretch of shoreline popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: School might employ such caution on a trek abroad

parts.note: care means caution

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A school urges caution on pupils going on a trek overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor who looks after a building is a staff member a school would hire.

clue.text: Protect quiet part of farm after head of farm leaves

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: leaves means the farm's first letter goes away

parts.note: a field is part of a farm

indicators.note: head of means the first letter

explanation.surface: Guard the peaceful farmland once the farmer departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard or screen from harm is a verb sense of the word for a defensive plate.

clue.text: Game finishing early in front of secure prison

indicators.note: in front of places the shortened game before the secure word
finishing early means the last letter of the game word is lost

parts.note: darts is a pub game of throwing at a board
to moor a boat is to secure it

explanation.surface: A game is cut short so that the prison can be locked down.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a well-known high-security prison on moorland in Devon, England.
explanation.definitionFit: HM Prison Dartmoor is a famous English jail, so the place name stands for a prison.

clue.text: Transformation of older Danish state

indicators.note: a transformation changes the form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political change to an ageing Danish nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest US state, in New England.

clue.text: Some never mind rats?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dismissive shrug: 'never mind', 'rats', both exclamations of mild annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats?' reads as the exclamation, like 'never mind'; the question mark flags it as the rodents instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are classic pests, and pests of that kind are collectively called by this word.

clue.text: Ban circle following old soldier

indicators.note: following puts the circle after the old soldier

parts.note: a vet is a veteran, an old soldier
the letter O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: A ring of protesters trails a war veteran, seeking a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: An official refusal or prohibition blocking a proposal is a synonym for a ban.

clue.text: Shell, maybe, producing scheme with French island

parts.note: a project is a scheme or plan
île is the French word for island

explanation.surface: A development scheme on a French island produces a seashell, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell' looks like a seashell, but it is an artillery shell, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artillery shell is one example of a missile fired from a gun.

clue.text: Top bank cheat on the loose? Sign of support needed

indicators.note: on the loose means running free and out of order, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A senior banker who defrauded people has escaped, and needs encouragement.
explanation.definitionFit: Patting someone between the shoulders is a gesture of congratulation or encouragement.

clue.text: Group required to follow score?

parts.note: looks like fans tracking a match result, but a musical score is read by an ensemble of players

explanation.surface: Supporters need to keep up with the match result.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ensemble of instrumental musicians plays from a written score.

clue.text: First person in Nice with a poor quality not admired

parts.note: je is French for I, and Nice is in France
lousy means poor or bad

explanation.surface: The leading figure in Nice has a lamentable trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' reads as the adjective but is the French city, pronounced 'neece'.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy and resentment are a disliked trait, a characteristic people do not praise.

clue.text: See fried food returned amid fare — fast food?

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the pieces sit inside the fare word

parts.note: good cheer is food and drink, so cheer can mean fare

indicators.note: fried, as cooked, signals the letters of see are knocked about
returned signals the food word is read backwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Fried food sent back in a restaurant where everything is fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' means food and drink, as in 'good cheer'; the scrambled see (by 'fried') and the food turned round (by 'returned') both sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty in a bun topped with a melted slice is a staple of fast-food chains.

clue.text: English remedy almost restricting fuss in country

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the shortened remedy goes round the fuss
almost means the last letter of the remedy word is dropped

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
ado means fuss

explanation.surface: A British cure that almost works causes a stir abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American nation on the equator, named after it.

clue.text: Tar in tumble at sea avoiding line

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor takes a tumble at sea while dodging a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tar' looks like a sailor, which 'at sea' supports, but it is the black road substance. 'avoiding line' drops L before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A black sticky petroleum material used on roads is tar-like pitch.

clue.text: Clean area providing free space

definitions.meaning: to clean a carpet with a suction cleaner
a region entirely empty of matter

explanation.surface: Tidying up an area to give everyone some room.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hoovering clean and a space devoid of any matter.

clue.text: Drink in Parisian eaterie, hearing Spanish cheer

parts.note: a café is a small Paris restaurant

indicators.note: hearing tells us the cheer is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: olé is the Spanish shout of approval

explanation.surface: In a Paris café, a diner hears a Spaniard shouting approval.
explanation.walkthrough: The French 'au lait' is pronounced like 'olé'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee with milk, a French-style beverage.

clue.text: Stupid person forgetting wife and friend

indicators.note: forgetting means the wife letter is left out

parts.note: wally is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A dim man forgets his wife and his friend.
explanation.walkthrough: A WALLY is everyday British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or supporter on the same side is a close synonym of a friend.

clue.text: An attitude turning up in fabulous writer

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the attitude word from bottom to top

parts.note: a pose is an attitude or stance

explanation.surface: A stance that surfaces in a storyteller's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of fables with talking animals is a writer of fables.

clue.text: Took part in tournament without justice and got supplanted

indicators.note: without means the justice letter is removed

parts.note: knights jousted in medieval tournaments
J is the abbreviation for a judge styled Justice

explanation.surface: A knight fought in the lists unfairly and was replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pushed out of a position by someone else is the sense of being removed or displaced.

clue.text: Terrible Saudi scam I exposed in foreign capital

indicators.note: terrible means in a dreadful state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letter I is taken as written and removed, the clue saying it is exposed

explanation.surface: A dreadful Saudi fraud is uncovered by a whistleblower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I exposed' means the I is taken away from SAUDISCAM before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Syria, a city abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: A German in lake lacking in strength

indicators.note: in puts the A and German inside the lake word

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: A German swimming in a lake is feeling weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty or feeble, something thin and insufficient, describes a weak quantity.

clue.text: Smart photo and case for photography

parts.note: a snap is a quick photo

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: A sharp photo and a carrying case for camera kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish dress is called smart or crisp, as in a sharp, well-turned-out outfit.
